title: Strategies for late phase preclinical and early clinical trials of senolytics - ScienceDirect
abstract: Accumulation of senescent cells is associated with age-related diseases and disorders. Senolytics and senomorphics are potential interventions for delaying, preventing, or treating age-related dysfunction. Senolytics show efficacy in pre-clinical and early clinical trials. Cellular senescence and the hallmarks of aging contribute to age-related disease and dysfunction. Accumulation of senescent cells is associated with frailty, cardiovascular disease, obesity, diabetes, cognitive decline, and other age- and/or chronic disease-related disorders, suggesting that senescent cells are a target for intervention. Early preclinical data using senolytics, agents that target senescent cells, show promising results in several aging and disease models. The first in-human trials using the senolytic combination of Dasatinib and Quercetin indicated reduced senescent cell burden in adipose tissue of diabetic kidney disease patients and improved physical function in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. These results from preclinical and early clinical trials illustrate the potential of senolytics to alleviate age-related dysfunction and diseases. However, multiple clinical trials across different aging and disease models are desperately needed.
